scope: Proposition 4.2 (Sampling from independent Brownian paths) of the manuscript “The free uniform spanning forest is a factor of IID” (preprints/The-free-uniform-spanning-forest-is-a-factor-of-IID-September-25-2026/The-free-uniform-spanning-forest-is-a-factor-of-IID-September-25-2026.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 231 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 478f5137621e0b3b), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 12. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let ν be a probability law on {0, 1}I, where I is countable, and for each i choose finite sets Sn(i) increasing to I. Interpret the finite-tilt functions (2.7) and the limsup drift (2.9) with this law and these sets. Suppose that the finite-tilt functions bi,Sn(i)(t, ·) are L-Lipschitz in the supremum norm on their finite fields, with one constant 0 ≤ L < ∞ for all i, n and t ≥ 0. Then the drift has the Borel solution map of Lemma 4.1, and the Borel map Ψ : CI −→ {0, 1}I defined by Ψi(w) = 1  lim sup n→∞ Zi(w)(n) n > 1 2  (4.5) sends the law of independent standard Brownian paths to ν. The map Ψ inherits every coordinate relabeling equivariance of the drift.
